package_info.package_versions: Any version uploaded after initial approval (malicious update)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is considered malicious because it is intentionally crafted to exploit a vulnerability in Jenkins' plugin update process, allowing attackers to inject cross-site scripting (XSS) payloads into the plugin metadata. This enables remote code execution or credential theft on Jenkins servers, even if the plugin is not installed, simply by viewing the Available Plugin Manager page.

execution_context.trigger: plugin update (metadata fetch) / admin UI page load
execution_context.file_location: Jenkins plugin HPI file (version attribute) → Update Center JSON → Jenkins admin web UI

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a Jenkins administrator opens the Available Plugin Manager page, the code executes a JavaScript payload embedded in the plugin metadata, which can steal credentials or execute arbitrary actions in the context of the admin session.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding executable JavaScript in metadata fields is a classic XSS technique, especially dangerous in admin interfaces.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Plugin metadata should never contain executable code; it should be plain text describing the plugin version.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use for executable code in version metadata; all such cases are suspicious.
key_indicators: Presence of <script> tags in metadata fields
Unexpected JavaScript in plugin version or description attributes
Execution of code on page load without user interaction

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads a benign plugin to the Jenkins Update Center to gain approval.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to upload updates to the same plugin.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads a malicious update with an XSS payload in the version attribute of the plugin HPI file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious metadata is stored in the Update Center JSON.

attack_chain.action: Jenkins servers fetch the updated plugin metadata from the Update Center.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious payload is now present in local plugin metadata.

attack_chain.action: Jenkins administrator opens the Available Plugin Manager page, triggering the XSS payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of attacker-controlled JavaScript in the admin's browser session (credential theft, remote code execution, etc.)

behavioral_signatures: Presence of <script> or other HTML tags in plugin metadata fields
Execution of JavaScript from plugin metadata in the Jenkins admin UI
Unexpected network requests initiated from the admin UI page
file_indicators: Jenkins Update Center JSON files containing script tags in version or description fields
HPI plugin files with non-standard metadata content
network_indicators: Outbound requests from Jenkins admin UI to attacker-controlled domains
Unexpected requests triggered by admin UI page loads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan plugin metadata (both in HPI files and Update Center JSON) for embedded script tags or suspicious HTML/JavaScript. Monitor Jenkins admin UI for execution of JavaScript not originating from official sources. Alert on any network requests initiated from the admin UI to untrusted domains, especially during plugin management operations.
